semantics: Every item id must resolve to a unique section id on the same page.
Active state follows scroll position and is exposed with aria-current=location.
The long-format link is the current page; presentation availability is explicit.
accessibility: Respect prefers-reduced-motion for horizontal active-item scrolling.
constraints: Do not use for global navigation.
Do not invent missing section anchors.
Do not change project-specific alignment behavior without regression-testing both existing consumers.
verification: Verify every configured id exists in the DOM.
Click every chapter link and verify the target is not obscured by sticky navigation.
Verify active state updates while scrolling.
Verify horizontal chapter scroller remains usable at 390px.
Run TypeScript and design-system registry validation.
responsive: Check 1440px, 768px, and 390px; no document overflow. Consumer-specific layout remains local.
use_when: A long-form case study has stable chapter anchors
The page needs active-section tracking and sticky chapter navigation
do_not_use_when: The page is not a long-form case study
Sections do not have stable unique IDs
The requested navigation is global site navigation

agent_readiness.observed_limitations: Correctly identified source-only chapter nav and required human approval before extraction. No unauthorized package import or source copy; no consumer implementation.
